title: Prime-to-ell uniformization reduces to marked nodal quotient models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. Consider the following assertion about marked nodal quotient models. Let $Y$ be an affine integral excellent regular Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension, with $\ell$ invertible, and let $T\subseteq Y$ be the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. Let $G$ be a finite group of order a power of $\ell$. Let $b:Y'\to Y$ be finite, with $Y'$ integral excellent and normal, such that, for $V=Y\setminus T$, $V'=b^{-1}V\to V$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor and $Y'$ is the normalization of $Y$ in its function field $\kappa(V')$. Let $f:C\to Y'$ be a $G$-equivariant projective flat finitely presented morphism, with $C$ integral excellent separated Noetherian, whose geometric fibres are nonempty connected curves smooth except for ordinary double points, and which is smooth over $V'$. An ordinary double point has completed geometric fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Let $D\subset C$ be a $G$-stable effective Cartier divisor, finite etale over $Y'$ and contained in the smooth locus of $f$. Assume the action on $C$ is admissible, meaning every orbit lies in an affine open, and let $\pi:C\to X=C/G$ be its finite scheme quotient, with $X$ integral excellent Noetherian. Scheme quotient here means the orbit-space quotient, with structure sheaf $(\pi_*\mathcal O_C)^G$. Put $B=|D|\cup f^{-1}b^{-1}T$. Let $E\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor such that $\pi^{-1}|E|\subseteq B$. The assertion is that there are an integral regular Noetherian scheme $R$ and a proper birational morphism $r:R\to X$ for which $r^{-1}|E|$ is the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. Birational means inducing an isomorphism on dense open subschemes.

If this assertion holds for every such marked nodal quotient model, then for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $S$ with $\ell$ invertible and every nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset S$, there is a finite covering family $(q_i:T_i\to S)$ in the topology of $\ell'$-alterations, with each $T_i$ regular Noetherian and $q_i^{-1}Z$ the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. In particular $q_i$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, hence of finite type.

Conventions: schemes, reduced schemes, Noetherian rings, excellence, regularity, integral schemes, properness, finite type and effective Cartier ideals are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]; boundaries and alteration coverings are as in [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Finite morphisms, projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, etaleness, geometric fibres, normalization, Galois torsors and Krull dimension are as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sc-normalization], [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Separated means that the diagonal into $C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}C$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Normalization in the indicated finite extension $L$ of the function field means the scheme obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the integral closure of each affine coordinate domain in $L$; thus the extension field, rather than just the original function field, is used.
